question_text: Which architectural smell indicates a violation of the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)?

options.text: Classes implementing interfaces with empty or `UnsupportedOperationException` stub methods
A class having more than 5 private variables
High test coverage on polymorphic classes

answer_explanation: When a class is forced to implement interface methods it does not need (throwing unsupported exceptions or leaving empty bodies), the interface is too fat, violating ISP.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: When a class is forced to implement interface methods it does not need (throwing unsupported exceptions or leaving empty bodies), the interface is too fat, violating ISP.

criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
